At present two prominent lawsuits concern ownership of the waters of the Bighorn River (Crow Indian Reservation) and the Tongue River (Northern Cheyenne Reservation).
On the Federal side, the Bureau of Reclamation assumes water management jurisdiction for impounded waters in reservoirs constructed by the Bureau. As of September 25, 1973, they had executed 19 industrial water marketing contracts with energy companies, totalling 623 thousand acre feet from the Yellowtail reservoir and 85 thousand acre feet from the Boysen reservoir.
The following discussion briefly discusses the legal and jurisdictional complexity of the issues involved. For further information the reader is referred to DES-75-2, Projected Coal Development, Crow Indian Reservation, BIA, 1975.
Indian Water Rights
The treaties with the Indians are generally silent about rights to use of water, but the Indians' water rights have been established by judicial decree. There have been a series of cases which involve the doctrine of the federal reserved right to the use of the water which has been withdrawn or reserved by the Federal Sovereign for specific purposes such as Indian Reservations, parks, forests, fish and wildlife refuges and military posts.
